readings.title: Pursuit and Betrayal
readings.subtitle: The Covenant at Horesh and the Ziphites' Treachery
readings.text: [1 Samuel 23:13] Then Dawid and his men, about six hundred, rose up and departed from Qe'ilah and went wherever they could go. And it was reported to Sha'ul that Dawid had escaped from Qe'ilah, so he ceased going out. [14] And Dawid stayed in the wilderness in strongholds, and remained in the mountains in the Wilderness of Ziph. And Sha'ul sought him every day, but <dn>Elohim</dn> did not give him into his hand. [15] And Dawid saw that Sha'ul had come out to seek <dn>את</dn> his life. And Dawid was in the Wilderness of Ziph in a forest. [16] And Yonathan, Sha'ul's son, rose up and went to Dawid in the forest and strengthened <dn>את</dn> his hand in <dn>Elohim</dn>. [17] And he said to him, “Do not fear, for the hand of Sha'ul my father is not going to find you. And you are to be sovereign over Yisra'el, and I am to be next to you. Even my father Sha'ul knows that.” [18] So the two of them made a covenant before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Dawid stayed in the forest, and Yonathan went to his own house. [19] And the Ziphites came up to Sha'ul at Gibeah, saying, “Is Dawid not hiding with us in strongholds in the forest, in the hill of Hakilah, which is on the south of Yeshimon? [20] “And now, O sovereign, come down according to all the desire of your being to come down, and our part is to surrender him into the sovereign’s hand.” [21] And Sha'ul said, “Blessed are you of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for you have compassion on me. [22] “Please go, make certain again, and know and see <dn>את</dn> the place where his hiding place is, who has seen him there. For I have been told that he is very crafty. [23] “And see and know of all the lurking places where he hides. And you shall return to me with certainty, then I shall go with you. And it shall be, if he is in the land, that I shall search for <dn>את</dn> him throughout all the thousands of Yehudah.” [24] And they rose up and went to Ziph before Sha'ul, while Dawid and his men were in the Wilderness of Ma'on, in the desert plain on the south of Yeshimon. [25] And Sha'ul and his men went to seek him, and they reported it to Dawid, so he went down to the rock, and stayed in the Wilderness of Ma'on. And Sha'ul heard it and pursued Dawid in the Wilderness of Ma'on. [26] And Sha'ul went on one side of the mountain, and Dawid and his men on the other side of the mountain. And Dawid was hurrying to get away from Sha'ul, for Sha'ul and his men were surrounding Dawid and his men, to catch them. [27] And a messenger came to Sha'ul, saying, “Hurry and come, for the Philistines have invaded the land!” [28] So Sha'ul turned back from pursuing Dawid, and went to meet the Philistines. Therefore they called that place Sela Hammahleqoth. [29] And Dawid went up from there and stayed in strongholds at Ěn Geḏi.

readings.title: A Maskil of Dawid
readings.subtitle: When the Ziphites Betrayed Him
readings.text: [Psalm 54:1] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, save me by <dn>Your Name</dn>, And rightly rule me by <dn>Your</dn> might. [2] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, hear my prayer; Listen to the words of my mouth. [3] For strangers have risen up against me, And fierce men have sought my life; They have not set <dn>Elohim</dn> before them. Selah. [4] See, <dn>Elohim</dn> is my helper; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with those who support my life. [5] <dn>He</dn> repays evil to my enemies. Cut them off in <dn>Your</dn> truth. [6] I slaughter to <dn>You</dn> voluntarily; I praise <dn>Your Name</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for it is good. [7] For <dn>He</dn> has delivered me out of all distress; And my eye has looked upon my enemies.

readings.title: Mercy in the Cave
readings.subtitle: Dawid Spares Sha'ul at Ěn Geḏi
readings.text: [1 Samuel 24:1] And it came to be, when Sha'ul had returned from following the Philistines, that it was reported to him, saying, “See, Dawid is in the Wilderness of Ěn Geḏi.” [2] And Sha'ul took <dn>את</dn> three thousand chosen men from all Yisra'el, and went to seek <dn>את</dn> Dawid and his men on the rocks of the wild goats. [3] And he came to the sheepfolds by the way, and a cave was there. And Sha'ul went in to attend to <dn>את</dn> his needs, and Dawid and his men were sitting in the recesses of the cave. [4] And the men of Dawid said to him, “See, the day of which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to you, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it seems good in your eyes.’</dq> ” And Dawid rose up and softly cut off <dn>את</dn> the corner of Sha'ul's robe. [5] And it came to be afterward that Dawid’s heart struck him because he had cut <dn>את</dn> Sha'ul's robe. [6] And he said to his men, “Far be it from me, by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I should do <dn>את</dn> this matter to my master, the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [7] And Dawid restrained <dn>את</dn> his servants with these words, and did not allow them to rise against Sha'ul. And Sha'ul got up from the cave and went on his way. [8] And Dawid rose up afterward, and went out of the cave, and called out to Sha'ul, saying, “My master the sovereign!” And Sha'ul looked behind him, and Dawid bowed his face to the earth, and did obeisance. [9] And Dawid said to Sha'ul, “Why do you listen to <dn>את</dn> the words of men who say, ‘See, Dawid is seeking your evil’? [10] “See, this day your eyes have seen that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave you today into my hand in the cave, and someone said to kill you. But my eye pitied you, and I said, ‘I do not stretch out my hand against my master, for he is the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ [11] “And my father, see! Yes, see <dn>את</dn> the corner of your robe in my hand! For in that I cut off <dn>את</dn> the corner of your robe, and did not kill you, know and see that there is neither evil nor rebellion in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, while you are hunting <dn>את</dn> my life to take it. [12] “Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> judge between you and me, and let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> revenge me on you, but my hand is not against you. [13] “As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Wrong comes from the wrongdoers.’ But my hand is not against you. [14] “After whom has the sovereign of Yisra'el come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea? [15] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be judge, and rightly rule between you and me, and see and plead <dn>את</dn> my case, and rightly rule me out of your hand.” [16] And it came to be, when Dawid had finished speaking <dn>את</dn> these words to Sha'ul, that Sha'ul said, “Is this your voice, my son Dawid?” And Sha'ul lifted up his voice and wept. [17] And he said to Dawid, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, while I have rewarded you with evil. [18] “And you have shown this day how you have dealt well with me, for when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> surrendered me into your hand, you did not kill me. [19] “For if a man finds <dn>את</dn> his enemy, does he let him get away safely? Therefore let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> reward you with good for what you have done to me this day. [20] “And now I know that you shall certainly reign, and that the reign of Yisra'el shall be established in your hand. [21] “And now, swear to me by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that you do not cut off <dn>את</dn> my seed after me, nor destroy <dn>את</dn> my name from my father’s house.” [22] And Dawid swore to Sha'ul, and Sha'ul went home, but Dawid and his men went up to the stronghold.

readings.title: Nabal's Folly
readings.subtitle: The Death of Shemu'el and Dawid's Request Denied
readings.text: [1 Samuel 25:1] And Shemu’ĕl died, and all Yisra'el gathered together and lamented for him, and buried him at his home in Ramah. And Dawid rose up and went down to the Wilderness of Paran. [2] And there was a man in Ma'on whose work was in Karmel, and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. And he was shearing <dn>את</dn> his sheep in Karmel. [3] And the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife Aḇigayil. And she was a woman of good understanding and beautiful appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his doings. And he was of the house of Kalĕḇ. [4] And Dawid heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing <dn>את</dn> his sheep. [5] So Dawid sent ten young men, and Dawid said to the young men, “Go up to Karmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name. [6] “And you shall say this, ‘To life! Peace be to you, and peace to your house, and peace to all that you have! [7] ‘And now, I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds were with us, and we did not harm them, nor was there any missing from them all the days they were in Karmel. [8] ‘Ask your young men, and let them declare to you. Therefore let my young men find favour in your eyes, for we come on a glad day. Please give <dn>את</dn> whatever comes to your hand to your servants and to your son Dawid.’ ” [9] And Dawid’s young men came and spoke to Nabal according to all these words in the name of Dawid, and waited. [10] But Nabal answered Dawid’s servants, and said, “Who is Dawid, and who is the son of Yishai? There are many servants today who break away, each one from his master. [11] “And should I take <dn>את</dn> my bread and <dn>את</dn> my water and <dn>את</dn> my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men whom I do not know where they are from?” [12] So Dawid’s young men turned <dn>את</dn> their way and went back, and came and reported to him according to all these words. [13] And Dawid said to his men, “Every man gird on <dn>את</dn> his sword.” And every man girded on <dn>את</dn> his sword, and Dawid also girded on <dn>את</dn> his sword. And about four hundred men went with Dawid, and two hundred stayed with the baggage. [14] And one of the young men declared to Aḇigayil, Nabal’s wife, saying, “See, Dawid sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, and he screamed at them. [15] “But the men were very good to us, and we were not harmed, nor did we miss any object all the days we went with them, while we were in the fields. [16] “They were a wall to us both by night and day, all the days we were with them tending <dn>את</dn> the sheep. [17] “And now, know and see what you should do, for evil is plotted against our master and against all his household. For he is such a son of Beliya'al that no one is able to speak to him.” [18] And Aḇigayil hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, and two skin bottles of wine, and five sheep already dressed, and five seahs of roasted grain, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and put them on donkeys, [19] and said to her servants, “Pass over before me, see, I am coming after you.” But she did not declare it to her husband Nabal. [20] And it came to be, as she rode on the donkey, that she went down under cover of the hill, and see, Dawid and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them. [21] Now Dawid had said, “In vain I have guarded <dn>את</dn> all that this one has in the wilderness, so that naught was missed of all that belongs to him, and he has repaid me evil for good. [22] “<dn>Elohim</dn> do so, and more also, to the enemies of Dawid, if I leave one male of all who belong to him by morning light.”

readings.title: Abigayil's Intercession
readings.subtitle: Wisdom Prevents Bloodshed
readings.text: [1 Samuel 25:23] And when Aḇigayil saw <dn>את</dn> Dawid, she hastened to dismount from the donkey, and fell on her face before Dawid, and bowed down to the ground, [24] and fell at his feet and said, “On me, my master, on me let this crookedness be! And please let your female servant speak in your ears, and hear <dn>את</dn> the words of your female servant. [25] “Please, let not my master regard this man of Beliya'al, Nabal. For as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your female servant, did not see <dn>את</dn> the young men of my master whom you sent. [26] “And now, my master, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives and as your being lives, since <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has held you back from coming to bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand, now then, let your enemies and those who seek evil for my master be as Nabal. [27] “And now this blessing which your female servant has brought to my master, let it be given to the young men who follow my master. [28] “Please forgive the transgression of your female servant. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly make a steadfast house for my master, because my master fights the battles of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and evil is not found in you throughout your days. [29] “And if anyone rises up to pursue you and seek <dn>את</dn> your life, then the life of my master shall be bound in the bundle of the living with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. But the lives of your enemies <dn>He</dn> shall sling out, as from the pocket of a sling. [30] “And it shall be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does for my master according to all <dn>את</dn> the good that <dn>He</dn> has spoken concerning you, and shall appoint you ruler over Yisra'el, [31] “that this shall be no cause of stumbling or a staggering of heart to my master, either to have shed blood without cause, or for my master to have avenged himself. And when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has dealt well with my master, then remember <dn>את</dn> your female servant.” [32] And Dawid said to Aḇigayil, “Blessed is <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra'el, who sent you this day to meet me! [33] “And blessed is your good sense and blessed are you, because you have kept me this day from coming to bloodshed and from avenging myself with my own hand. [34] “For indeed, as <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra'el lives, who has kept me back from hurting <dn>את</dn> you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, surely by morning light no male would have been left to Nabal.” [35] Dawid then accepted from her hand <dn>את</dn> what she had brought him, and said to her, “Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and have respected your face.” [36] And Aḇigayil went to Nabal, and see, he was holding a feast in his house, like the feast of a sovereign. And Nabal’s heart was glad within him, for he was very drunk. So she declared to him naught, little or much, until morning light. [37] And it came to be in the morning, when the wine had gone from Nabal, and his wife had declared <dn>את</dn> these matters to him, that his heart died within him, and he became like a stone. [38] And it came to be, about ten days later, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> struck <dn>את</dn> Nabal, and he died.

readings.title: Dawid's New Wives
readings.subtitle: Abigayil and Ahino'am
readings.text: [1 Samuel 25:39] And Dawid heard that Nabal was dead, and he said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who has pleaded <dn>את</dn> the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> servant from evil! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has returned <dn>את</dn> the evil of Nabal on his own head.” And Dawid sent and spoke to Aḇigayil, to take her as his wife. [40] And the servants of Dawid went to Aḇigayil at Karmel, and spoke to her, saying, “Dawid has sent us to you, to take <dn>את</dn> you as his wife.” [41] And she rose up, bowed her face to the earth, and said, “Here is your female servant, as a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my master.” [42] And Aḇigayil hurried and rose and rode on a donkey, attended by five of her young women. And she followed the messengers of Dawid, and became his wife. [43] And Dawid had taken <dn>את</dn> Ahino'am of Yizre'el, and so both of them were his wives. [44] But Sha'ul had given <dn>את</dn> Mikal his daughter, Dawid’s wife, to Palti son of Layish, who was from Gallim.
